ceiling_directive: Prove matching local-asymptotic expected-diameter bounds for implementable confidence procedures over the panel class itself, deriving uniform integrability and coverage-boundary control rather than replacing estimated effects by exactly observed b.
improvement_directive: Transfer both honesty and unbounded expected-diameter risk from the finite-sample panel experiment to a bounded-spread local limit, then construct an implementable estimator-based kernel attaining the resulting lower bound. This must cover root-n-separated arrays and multiple-close-donor faces with the shared-control covariance retained.
critique: The advertised weak-separation panel frontier is not proved over the panel triangular-array experiment: the exact minimax value concerns a repaired experiment that observes b without noise and imposes a bounded effect spread. The transfer theorem expressly excludes the discontinuous coverage event and unbounded expected-diameter loss that define the claimed frontier, so neither its converse nor its attaining randomized kernel transfers to feasible panel inference. The panel results establish uniform coverage and fixed-separation oracle equivalence, but they provide no matching local-minimax expected-diameter characterization over root-n-separated arrays. The unrestricted full Gaussian model yields only an infinite-risk diagnosis, while the Mahalanobis theorem solves a fixed two-state restriction rather than the full panel problem. The TL;DR and scope disclose these limitations, so the shortfall is the narrower proved object rather than a stale assertion of a completed panel frontier.
